mission: Bridge the Game9K live-interaction product to the messy reality of creators, viewers, live platforms and commerce operations without losing a measurable viewer outcome.
product_principle: Ship the smallest field-ready mission slice, prove value with a creator, then productize the reusable delta.

three_whys.system_of_record: Normalized TikTok/YouTube live events, room team attribution, avatar proxy status and heat telemetry are the operational ground truth; the visible canvas is a projection.
three_whys.cost_of_inaction: A technically polished overlay that creators cannot connect, viewers cannot understand or operators cannot recover will not create live participation or commerce value.
three_whys.day_2_owner: Game9K Live Ops owns room health and incident response; Creator Success owns onboarding and UAT; Studio Engineering owns the reusable SDK and release gates.

stakeholders.outcome: Join a marble quickly, see a recognizable avatar, understand team impact and feel a fair late-race reversal.
stakeholders.evidence_of_value: join rate, avatar render rate, event-to-visual latency and heat completion

stakeholders.outcome: Connect a TikTok or YouTube room in minutes and use PK gifts as visible participation mechanics.
stakeholders.evidence_of_value: time to first room, UAT checklist, reconnect recovery and repeat heat rate

stakeholders.outcome: Diagnose upstream, queue, avatar and release failures without depending on the original engineer.
stakeholders.evidence_of_value: runbook coverage, alert ownership, incident time to acknowledge and replayable seed

stakeholders.outcome: Convert the field delta into a reusable, compliant Game9K capability without treating viewers as investors.
stakeholders.evidence_of_value: creator retention, gift participation, release integrity and G2 evidence

discovery_checklist.evidence: Creator/streamer is the field champion for each pilot room.
Real creator UAT and upstream platform availability remain external dependencies.
Metrics are defined below with owners and evidence sources.
G2 manifest, avatar allowlist/proxy and no-investment-to-play policy.
Socket.IO primary, SSE fallback, simulator/demo path.
G2 classification and existing U18 portal controls.
Room connection contract exists; production creator credentials are not stored in the repository.
Gateway binds 0.0.0.0 and browser-facing clients use relative URLs.
Telemetry is capped at 10 Hz for Marble Race and package gzip is below 125 KB.

delta.field_gap: Two creators need isolated rooms with authoritative team attribution and no cross-talk.
A live audience needs many recognizable participants, not a renamed single-player racer.
delta.proposed_glue: 120-marble capped engine, avatar proxy, density-aware Canvas renderer and normalized join/like/chat events.

delta.field_gap: A gift needs an immediate, legible social consequence rather than an opaque score mutation.
delta.proposed_glue: Team boost plus opponent obstacle with visible seed, event toast and between-heat queue.

success_metrics.definition: Minutes from receiving a Browser Source URL to a creator seeing a live heat with both room routes visible.
Percentage of normalized join/chat viewers that receive a marble before the join window closes.
success_metrics.evidence: Heat telemetry: marble_joined / normalized join-like events

success_metrics.definition: Time from normalized gift/chat receipt to the viewer-visible boost, toast or obstacle effect.
success_metrics.evidence: Room event timestamp and client telemetry sample

success_metrics.definition: A heat can be reproduced from its visible seed and event receipt without changing a finished result.
success_metrics.target: 100% deterministic obstacle layout; zero post-finish mutation

success_metrics.definition: Live Ops can identify a disconnected source, use the queue/replay controls and recover without an engineer.
success_metrics.evidence: KOL streaming guide and incident review

delivery_gates.exit_criteria: Champion, blocker, system of record, cost of inaction and Day-2 owner are named.
Marble package validates, tests pass, PK team contract is authoritative and standalone bundle is reproducible.
At least one TikTok creator and one YouTube creator complete the connection, heat, gift and recovery checklist.
validate/build/verify/decide pass and no security or bundle-budget violation is present.
Live Ops owns room health, creator onboarding, incident severity and weekly value review.

risks.title: No real creator UAT evidence is stored yet
risks.mitigation: Run a two-room pilot and attach anonymized setup/recovery evidence to the weekly summary.

risks.title: The repository has one confirmed dinosaur game; cyber-boss-raid is not assumed to be a dinosaur
risks.mitigation: Confirm the second dinosaur slug before applying a dinosaur-specific shared contract.

risks.title: TikTok or YouTube upstream behavior can change outside the repository
risks.mitigation: Keep simulator/demo input, Socket.IO/SSE fallback, normalized fixtures and reconnect runbook.

risks.title: Viewer names and avatar URLs are live user data
risks.mitigation: Use avatar allowlist/proxy, safe display fields, G2 portal controls and no-investment-to-play policy.

next_actions.title: Run a two-creator PK UAT with anonymized evidence
next_actions.definition_of_done: Setup, join, gift-to-opponent, reconnect and next-heat queue are recorded for TikTok and YouTube.

next_actions.title: Instrument event-to-visual latency and viewer join rate
next_actions.definition_of_done: A redacted telemetry sample reports p50/p95 latency and join conversion per heat.

next_actions.title: Publish the Day-2 Live Ops runbook and escalation rota
next_actions.definition_of_done: Five failure modes have detection, owner, mitigation and recovery evidence.

next_actions.definition_of_done: A confirmed slug and owner are added before dinosaur-specific scope is expanded.
